crossRefs.note: He said, “While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, ‘Who knows whether Yahweh will not be gracious…
Call on me in the day of trouble. I will deliver you, and you will honor me.”
Yahweh, in trouble they have visited you. They poured out a prayer when your chastening was on them.
“Yet even now,” says Yahweh, “turn to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.”
Who knows whether God will not turn and relent, and turn away from his fierce anger, so that we might not perish?”
“Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Susa, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night…
When I wept and I fasted, that was to my reproach.
In that day, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, called to weeping, to mourning, to baldness, and to dressing in sackcloth;
He was without sight for three days, and neither ate nor drank.
Then the king arose, and tore his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

people.name: David
people.line: Anointed king of Israel, ancestor of Jesus Christ

translations.web: David therefore begged God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night on the ground.
translations.bsb: David pleaded with God for the boy. He fasted and went into his house and spent the night lying in sackcloth on the ground.
translations.kjv: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
